ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, it is known that $BA=BC$, $\angle B=120^\circ$, and the perpendicular bisector $DE$ of $AB$ intersects $AC$ at point D. If $AC=6\,cm$, what is the length of $AD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect $BD$,\\
since the perpendicular bisector $DE$ of $AB$ intersects $AC$ at point D,\\
it follows that $AD=BD$,\\
hence $\angle A=\angle ABD$,\\
since $BA=BC$, $\angle B=120^\circ$,\\
it follows $\angle A=\angle C=\frac{1}{2}\left(180^\circ-120^\circ\right)=30^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ABD=30^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle CBD=90^\circ$,\\
thus $CD=2BD$,\\
hence $CD=2AD$,\\
thus $AC=AD+CD=AD+2AD=3AD$,\\
further, since $AC=6\text{cm}$,\\
it follows $AD=\boxed{2\text{cm}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC, with A at the lower left, C at the lower right, B above, and AC as the base; point D is located on the base AC; a straight line DE passes through D and intersects side AB at E, and a right-angle mark is drawn at E, indicating that DE is perpendicular to AB. Reasoning: According to the problem, draw and connect BD. Because DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB, and D is on DE, D has equal distances to points A and B, that is, AD=BD. Also because BA=BC and ∠B=120°, triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠A=∠C=(180°-120°)/2=30°. D is on AC, therefore ∠DAB=30°. In triangle ABD, AD=BD, so the base angles ∠DAB=∠ABD=30°. Thus ∠DBC=∠ABC-∠ABD=120°-30°=90°. In triangle BCD, ∠DBC=90°, and ∠BCD=∠C=30°, so it is a 30°-60°-90° right triangle, and the hypotenuse CD is equal to 2 times the side BD opposite 30°, that is, CD=2BD. Also BD=AD, so CD=2AD. From AC=AD+CD=AD+2AD=3AD=6 cm, obtain AD=2 cm.
